classification.name: FRAMEWORK_KERNEL_DEFECT
classification.primary_cause: admitted fully PRE_SATISFIED (STORY-01-05's developer had implemented `verify`): developer_call_permitted false, no developer request, candidate = parent, plan-drift emitted, the obligation's VerifiedProof SATISFIED with agreement — everything RFC §14 and §17 name for a story that 'ends STORY_ALREADY_SATISFIED'. The engineering-adequacy stage then ran over a story no developer had been asked to work on: the story-owned test file the harness declares (tests/test_<story>.py) does not exist, which the kernel typed STORY_TESTS_NOT_COLLECTABLE, developer-caused, relevance IRRELEVANT -> INADEQUATE, owner DEVELOPER, developer_chargeable true; under the blocking tests policy that is TESTS_INADEQUATE (DEVELOPER, retryable): one retry charged to the DEVELOPER budget — with no developer call possible, so the retry repeated the same events — then ROLLBACK. The reproducer in this record shows the same rollback and the same charged retry when the story's tests DO exist and pass at the parent (VACUOUS and IRRELEVANT, because the product diff is empty), so the harness's test-path convention is not the cause: under TestsPolicy(blocking=True) a fully PRE_SATISFIED story does not commit, whether its tests are absent (LedgerLock) or present and passing (reproducer). RFC §14: a PRE_SATISFIED obligation MUST 'consume no developer budget' and 'MUST NOT require that correct code be made incorrect' (the only way to make the tests non-vacuous here); §17: 'a commit MUST NOT depend on a developer test verdict'; §15.3 lets a project make INADEQUATE block. The blocking stance is the benchmark harness's choice (no shipped default exists); the defect is the kernel's handling of that permitted stance on a story §14 says ends already satisfied. Two other readings exist and are the Owner's to weigh: C (the stance is qualification-profile-specific and a non-blocking stance commits the story) and E (the RFC does not say how §15.3 applies to a story with no developer call). This record takes A because a legal policy value makes the kernel contradict a §14 MUST, and the ruling forbids choosing the convenient class.

STORY-02-01.can_affect_an_ordinary_v2_user: YES for any integrator who chooses a blocking tests policy: every fully PRE_SATISFIED story rolls back and spends a DEVELOPER retry.
